column2: Master of Arts in Applied Anthropology
column16: To be considered for admission to the Master of Arts in Applied Anthropology degree program, prospective students must have a bachelor’s degree in Anthropology or a related field (e.g., Sociology, Geography, History, Political Science, Philosophy, Religious Studies, Women’s and Gender Studies, Environmental Studies). Applicants with a bachelor’s degree in a non-related field may be considered for admission if their undergraduate training or professional experience has provided appropriate background. Students who are admitted but lack sufficient background in anthropology may be required to complete preparatory coursework. Application to the MA in Applied Anthropology program is a two-part process requiring applicants to apply to both the Toulouse Graduate School and the Department of Anthropology. You must provide the following materials to the Toulouse Graduate School: An official transcript from each college or university you have attended. Official GRE scores (verbal, quantitative, analytical writing). You must provide the following materials to the Department of Anthropology: A current curriculum vita (CV) or resume. A Statement of Purpose that explains your academic and research background, your interest in the MA in Applied Anthropology program at UNT, and your career goals, as well as an identification of one or more faculty members with whom you would like to work and why (approximately 1,000 words). A writing sample (e.g., a paper or thesis from an undergraduate course). Three letters of recommendation. For international applicants whose native language is not English, a minimum TOEFL score of 79 (internet-based), IELTS score of 6.0, or PTE score of 53 is required. The departmental recommendation is a minimum TOEFL score of 90 (internet-based).
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences (CLASS)
column47: The Master of Arts (MA) program in Applied Anthropology offers two tracks: Cultural Anthropology and Public Archeology. The MA program helps students develop skills in grant writing, research design, project management, and cultural resource management. Students can also participate in fieldwork, internships, and laboratory research. The program prepares students for careers in cultural resource management, museums, non-profit agencies, community advocacy organizations, government agencies, international development, and more. A PhD in Applied Anthropology is also available.

column2: Master of Arts in Art Education
column16:
In addition to the requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School, applicants for the MA in Art Education must meet the following program requirements:
* A strong interest in art education.
* Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA in undergraduate work.
* Resume or CV
* Statement of purpose explaining your interest in art education and professional goals.
* Two letters of recommendation, with at least one from a university faculty member.
* Writing sample of an academic paper completed during undergraduate or previous graduate work (5-10 pages).
* Portfolio of 10-15 images of recent artwork. Include a list of images (title, medium, dimensions, date). Applicants will upload their writing sample and portfolio to their personal Slideroom account, accessed through the application.
* Official GRE scores are not required for admission.
* International applicants must fulfill requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School regarding English proficiency.
column38: College of Visual Arts and Design
column47: The MA in Art Education allows students to tailor their graduate studies to suit their interests and career goals. Students choose courses from the fields of art education, art history, studio art and related areas. The program offers thesis and non-thesis options. Graduates are prepared for a range of professional opportunities as art educators in K-12 schools, community organizations, museums, galleries and other institutions.
column52: Texas Resident: ~$486/credit hour; Non-Resident: ~$1025/credit hour (based on 1-9 credit hours for 2023-2024 academic year)

column2: Master of Arts in Art History
column16:
In addition to the general admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School, applicants to the MA in Art History must meet the following departmental requirements:
1. An undergraduate major in art history or 18 semester hours of advanced courses in art history that are approved by the department.
2. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0.
3. Three letters of recommendation submitted directly to the Graduate School.
4. A statement of purpose (1,000 words maximum) outlining the student’s interests in art history and reasons for pursuing graduate study.
5. A writing sample (8-10 pages) that demonstrates the student’s ability to write critically and clearly about art history. This should be an essay written for an advanced undergraduate art history course.
6. A CV or resume.
7. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended.
8. GRE scores are NOT required for admission to the MA program in Art History.
column38: College of Visual Arts and Design
column47: The Master of Arts in Art History degree program offers two paths to completion: a thesis option and a non-thesis option. In both cases, the program is a 30-hour course of study for students interested in advanced work in art history. Students pursuing the M.A. in Art History work closely with faculty in their areas of interest, are involved in research and critical analysis, and have opportunities to develop their teaching skills and gain professional experience. The M.A. prepares students for careers in museums, galleries, and archives, as well as for further graduate study at the doctoral level.

column2: Master of Arts in Communication Studies
column16: Admission to the M.A. program is competitive. Successful applicants generally have an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or better and a combined Verbal and Quantitative score of 300 or better on the Graduate Record Examinations (GRE). The analytical writing score from the GRE is also taken into consideration. To apply for the M.A. in Communication Studies, you must submit the following: A completed application for graduate admission. Official transcripts of all college-level work. Official GRE scores (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing). A statement of purpose (1,000 words max) that explains your interest in the MA program in Communication Studies at UNT, your research interests, and your professional goals. A current resume or CV. A writing sample (e.g., a scholarly paper, a research paper, a chapter from an undergraduate thesis, etc.) that demonstrates your ability to write clearly and persuasively. For additional information, see the Communication Studies Graduate Catalog.
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
column46: Health Communication, Intercultural Communication, Mediated Communication
column47: The Master of Arts in Communication Studies program prepares students for a diverse range of careers in higher education, research, and for positions within private and public organizations. The program allows students to specialize within the areas of Health Communication, Intercultural Communication, and Mediated Communication, while preparing them for doctoral work. The curriculum helps students develop knowledge and skills in critical inquiry, research design, theory, and professional presentation within and beyond the communication discipline. Faculty expertise includes intercultural communication, health communication, rhetorical studies, media studies, organizational communication, and interpersonal communication.
column82: combined verbal and quantitative GRE score of at least 290 and an analytical writing score of at least 3.5

column2: Master of Arts in Creative Writing
column16: To be considered for admission to the MA in Creative Writing, applicants must meet the following requirements in addition to the general requirements for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. A minimum 3.0 grade point average on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Satisfactory scores on the Graduate Record Examination (GRE). Statement of Purpose that explains the applicant's reasons for wishing to pursue graduate study in Creative Writing, outlining previous experience in the field and discussing literary influences. Resume (or curriculum vitae) listing academic and professional achievements. Writing Sample of 15-25 pages of original fiction, poetry or creative nonfiction. Applicants must identify the genre of the writing sample. Three letters of recommendation from former professors or professionals who can attest to the applicant's academic abilities and/or professional aptitudes.
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
column47: The Master of Arts in Creative Writing at UNT provides advanced study in the writing of fiction, poetry, and literary nonfiction. Our program emphasizes work in one primary genre, as well as the study of literature and literary theory, culminating in the composition of a book-length manuscript or thesis. Graduates of our program teach creative writing and English at the high school and college levels, work in editing and publishing, or continue on to Ph.D. programs.

column2: Master of Arts in English
column16: To be considered for admission to the MA in English program, an applicant must satisfy the general requirements for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School, hold a bachelor’s degree with an undergraduate major in English, or at least 18 hours of upper-division English credit, including a minimum of three hours in American literature, three hours in British literature, and three hours in advanced writing. Applicants are also required to submit a personal statement (300-500 words) and a critical writing sample (8-10 pages) demonstrating their ability to formulate and support an argument about literary texts. Applicants must also provide three letters of recommendation from faculty members familiar with their academic work.
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
column47: The Master of Arts program in English at UNT provides graduate students with a rigorous, comprehensive education in literary studies. Students engage in advanced critical thinking and research, developing expertise in various literary periods, genres, and theoretical approaches. The curriculum emphasizes analytical skills, clear communication, and scholarly writing, preparing graduates for doctoral studies, teaching positions, and diverse professional careers.

column2: Master of Arts in History
column16: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School and the following program requirements: One official transcript of all college work. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and/or a 3.5 GPA on all graduate work. GRE revised General Test required. A minimum score of 153 on the verbal portion, 144 on the quantitative portion, and 4.0 on the analytical writing portion is recommended. A statement of purpose (1,000 words, double-spaced) describing your previous academic and/or professional training, the areas of history you propose to study at UNT, and your future career goals. A writing sample (8-15 pages, double-spaced) demonstrating your ability to conduct research and write a scholarly paper. Three letters of recommendation from former professors who are familiar with your academic work. Resume/CV (optional).
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences (Department of History)
column47: The Department of History offers a Master of Arts degree that provides advanced training in historical research and writing. The program prepares students for continued graduate work at the Ph.D. level or for a variety of public and private sector careers, including teaching at the community college level, work in museums, archives, or government agencies. Students select a major field (American History, European History, or Latin American History) and a minor field from a different region (American, European, or Latin American) or from a topical field (African History, Asian History, Ancient/Classical History, or Public History). Students also select a subfield, which may be a specific time period or a particular approach to history (e.g., gender history, environmental history, etc.).

column2: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies
column16: A formal application to The Graduate School and the Department of Interdisciplinary Studies. Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to The Graduate School. GRE is required.
column47:
The MA in Interdisciplinary Studies is a research-based, customizable graduate program that provides students with the opportunity to pursue an individualized course of study. The curriculum is constructed around three academic areas, or fields of study, chosen by the student. These fields of study draw from the rich and diverse faculty and departmental offerings across the university.
The MA in Interdisciplinary Studies is designed for students seeking a graduate program that transcends traditional disciplinary boundaries and fosters critical thinking, problem-solving, and cross-disciplinary communication skills. Graduates are prepared for careers that require adaptability, creativity, and the ability to synthesize knowledge from multiple perspectives.
Students work closely with an Interdisciplinary Studies faculty advisor and a faculty committee chosen by the student, ensuring personalized guidance throughout their academic journey.

column2: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Applied Gerontology
column16: Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate coursework. Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) general test is required. Statement of Purpose. Two letters of recommendation. Resume.

column40: Resident: $4,917.48/semester (for 9 credit hours); Non-Resident: $9,711.48/semester (for 9 credit hours)
column47: The Interdisciplinary Studies (M.A.) with a concentration in Applied Gerontology combines the expertise of UNT’s Gerontology program with the flexibility of the Interdisciplinary Studies M.A. The program is designed for students interested in working with older adults in a variety of settings, as well as those pursuing further graduate education in gerontology. Coursework is designed to provide students with a strong theoretical and practical understanding of gerontology.

column2: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Digital Social Science
column16: Completion of a bachelor's degree. A strong academic record, typically a GPA of 3.0 or higher. Two letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant's academic abilities and/or professional experience. A statement of purpose (approximately 500-750 words) that addresses: Why you are interested in the MAIS program and the Digital Social Science concentration specifically; How your academic and professional background has prepared you for this interdisciplinary program; Your research interests and career goals, and how this program aligns with them. A curriculum vitae or resume. GRE scores are NOT required.
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
column47: The Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies (MAIS) degree program is designed for students whose intellectual and professional interests require a unique combination of courses from three academic disciplines at UNT. This degree provides flexibility in course selection and research options. Students, with the help of a faculty advisory committee, design a plan of study that crosses departmental, college and institutional boundaries. The MAIS degree allows for flexibility in course selection and research options within areas such as Digital Humanities, Information Science, Music, Public Administration, Public Relations, Rehabilitation Counseling, Sociology, Technical Communication and Urban Planning.

column2: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Humanities
column16: Admission to the master’s program is open to applicants who hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School, which are listed in the Graduate Admissions section of this catalog. In addition to meeting the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School, applicants for the MA in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Humanities must submit: An essay (2-5 pages) explaining how the applicant's prior academic and/or professional experiences have prepared them for interdisciplinary study in the humanities and what they hope to achieve through the program. This essay serves as a writing sample and statement of purpose. Three letters of recommendation, at least two from university faculty familiar with the applicant’s academic performance. Official transcripts of all college-level work. An academic resume or curriculum vitae (CV) describing previous education, employment history and any other information relevant to graduate study. GRE Scores: Applicants whose undergraduate GPA is less than 3.0 must also submit official scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE). Applicants who are required to take the GRE must also include an unofficial copy of their scores in their application packet.
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
column47: The Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies (MAIS) is a custom-designed master's degree program that allows students to combine graduate-level courses from three academic disciplines into a unified program of study based on a central theme, problem or issue. The humanities concentration allows students to pursue courses related to Art, Dance, English, History, Journalism, Media Arts, Music, Philosophy and Religion, Second Language Acquisition, Sociology, and Technical Communication.
column101: Tuition Scholarships, Fellowships, Assistantships (Teaching, Research), Grants (Travel)

column2: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication
column16: You must meet the general requirements for admission to the graduate school and specific requirements for the M.A. in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication. General Admission Requirements: Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. (You may also be admitted if you demonstrate equivalent academic achievement.) An undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher in the last 60 undergraduate credit hours (or a minimum score on the GRE). Satisfactory performance on the GRE General Test, if required by the program. Degree-specific Admission Requirements: For the M.A. in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication, you must also: Possess a bachelor’s degree with a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum 3.0 GPA on 12 hours of graduate coursework (or a GRE total score of 292 with a minimum of 146 on both the verbal and quantitative sections and a 3.5 on the analytical writing section).
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences and the College of Visual Arts and Design
column47: Our Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication is available in a convenient 100% online format. In this program, you’ll focus on how humans communicate and interact with digital technologies to create virtual experiences. The digital communication concentration helps students understand and critically analyze digital communication and media, as well as design and develop digital interactive and virtual experiences. You'll learn about: Digital communication in society, Communication in digital environments, Virtual environments and experiences, Media and digital communication ethics, Interactive media theory, Research methods in digital communication. UNT offers students the opportunity to: Study with faculty from various departments and colleges across the university. Work with an interdisciplinary team to apply skills in a practical setting. Prepare for a career in interactive and virtual communication, marketing, public relations or digital media.

column2: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Program Leadership
column11: US Applicants: July 15 (for Fall admission); International Applicants: May 15 (for Fall admission)
column16:
Admission to the Interdisciplinary Studies, M.A. program requires the following:
*   GRE general test scores. Official GRE scores are required for all applicants.
*   Statement of purpose. Required.
*   Writing sample. Required.
*   Three letters of recommendation. Required.
*   Resume or curriculum vitae. Required.
*   Application to the Toulouse Graduate School. All prospective graduate students must apply for admission to UNT’s Toulouse Graduate School.
column47: UNT's Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Program Leadership prepares you to lead programs in a variety of settings. Organizations across all sectors (government, non-profit, corporate, educational) need skilled program leaders to plan, manage, evaluate and lead the initiatives that serve their missions. Program leadership is an evolving field that demands individuals with both conceptual and practical skills. In this concentration, you will explore the knowledge and skills necessary to be an effective program leader, including program planning, development, implementation, evaluation, fundraising, strategic planning, human resources, budgeting and assessment. Our unique curriculum allows students to integrate the study of program leadership with another area of interest such as business, communication, higher education, public administration or another field. It is a highly customizable degree that can be tailored to meet your specific career goals. We offer courses fully online.
column101: Merit-based, Tuition support, Research/Travel Grants, Assistantships (with tuition remission)

column2: Master of Arts in International Studies
column16: To be considered for admission to the M.A. program in International Studies, applicants should apply online through the Toulouse Graduate School and submit the following documents directly to the Toulouse Graduate School: Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Transcripts must be sent directly from the institution in a sealed envelope or through a secure electronic method to the Toulouse Graduate School. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to your academic ability and potential for success in graduate school. Letters of recommendation should be submitted directly by the recommenders to the Toulouse Graduate School. Statement of Purpose: A two-page (double-spaced) statement outlining your academic and professional goals, research interests, and reasons for pursuing graduate study in International Studies at UNT. The statement should demonstrate your writing ability and analytical skills. Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV): A current resume or CV highlighting your educational background, work experience, research projects, publications, presentations, and any other relevant experience. Writing Sample: An academic paper, essay, or research project (8-15 pages in length) that demonstrates your research, analytical, and writing skills. The writing sample should preferably be on a topic related to international studies or political science. GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores are NOT required for admission to the MA in International Studies program. For international applicants, proof of English language proficiency is required (e.g., TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, Duolingo English Test scores). Please refer to the Toulouse Graduate School website for specific requirements.
column38: College of Liberal Arts & Social Sciences
column39: $5,780.00 - $10,244.00/Semester (based on 9 credit hours, 2024-2025 rates for Texas Resident / Non-Resident)
column47: The Master of Arts in International Studies (MAIS) program at the University of North Texas provides students with an interdisciplinary understanding of global issues and prepares them for careers in international affairs, government, non-governmental organizations, and further graduate study. Students develop advanced analytical skills, critical thinking, and a comprehensive understanding of international political, economic, and cultural dynamics. The curriculum is designed to offer both breadth in international studies and the opportunity for specialization through elective courses and thesis/professional paper options.
column52: $530.60 - $938.60/credit hour (2024-2025 rates for Texas Resident / Non-Resident)

column2: Master of Arts in Journalism
column16: Review the University requirements for graduate admission. Official GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores. If required by the department, official GRE scores must be sent directly from the Educational Testing Service (ETS) to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School (code 6480). For more information, visit the GRE General Test website. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. International students may be required to submit official TOEFL or IELTS scores. 3.0 GPA minimum in the last 60 undergraduate hours. Writing sample – maximum 10 pages. Please choose work that reflects your best writing ability, whether academic or professional. If you do not have any writing that you feel showcases your best work, consider writing a new piece specifically for this application. Resume (Required). Statement of Purpose (Required). Three (3) letters of recommendation.
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
column47: The Master of Arts in Journalism program gives students the opportunity to advance their knowledge and skills to lead and innovate in the ever-evolving fields of media and communication. Students gain expertise in media theory, research, ethics, and practices across a variety of traditional and emerging platforms. Through advanced coursework and scholarly inquiry, students develop a deep understanding of the role of journalism in a democratic society, critical thinking skills, and proficiency in creating high-quality, impactful content. This program is ideal for professionals seeking career advancement, individuals preparing for doctoral studies, or those looking to transition into the dynamic world of journalism and strategic communication. Graduates are prepared for leadership roles in news organizations, public relations, advertising, media management, content creation, and related fields, or for further academic pursuits.
column101: Texas Public Education Grant (TPEG), Graduate Assistantships

column2: Master of Arts in Media Industry and Critical Studies
column16: Admission to the master’s program in Media Industry and Critical Studies is contingent on admission to the Toulouse Graduate School and on the recommendation of the department. The decision to admit a student to the program is based on a holistic review of all application materials and considers factors related to the applicant’s background and aptitude for graduate study in media studies. Applicants must satisfy the following additional requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants are not required to have an undergraduate degree in media studies or a related field. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to the applicant’s academic and/or professional abilities. A statement of purpose (approximately 500-750 words) that describes the applicant’s academic interests and goals, relevant experiences, and reasons for pursuing graduate study in Media Industry and Critical Studies at UNT. A writing sample (e.g., an academic paper, professional report, or published article) that demonstrates the applicant’s analytical and writing abilities. Official GRE scores are not required. A current résumé or curriculum vitae (CV).
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences (CLASS)
column40: Estimated $15,316/Year for Texas Residents (Fall 2024, 18 credit hours)
column47: The Master of Arts (MA) in Media Industry and Critical Studies prepares students for further graduate study in media studies or related fields, as well as for work in a variety of industries (including the media industry) that require advanced analytical, communication, and research skills. Drawing upon a critical and interdisciplinary approach, the MA curriculum grounds students in the history, theory, and methods of media studies, while also providing them with knowledge of the shifting landscape of media industries and their cultural, economic, and political significance. Required coursework provides a foundation in media industry and critical studies research. Students then choose electives from a wide range of courses in media theory and history, media industries and institutions, and media and culture. The program provides two options for completing the MA: the thesis option and the professional paper option. In consultation with a graduate advisor, students choose the option best suited to their academic and professional goals.

column2: Master of Arts in Philosophy
column16: To apply for this program, you must apply to the Toulouse Graduate School through the ApplyUNT portal. The following items are required for your application: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Three letters of recommendation addressing your academic abilities. A statement of purpose outlining your philosophical interests and your reasons for wishing to pursue graduate study in philosophy at UNT. A writing sample of 10-20 pages (preferably philosophical).
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
column47: This program is designed for students whose intellectual interests are best served by broad, rather than highly specialized, study within philosophy. Students will explore traditional areas of philosophy (e.g., epistemology, metaphysics, ethics, logic, history of philosophy) and will gain an awareness of current work in these areas. The program provides a broad-based, rigorous education in philosophy suitable for students who wish to teach philosophy at community colleges, pursue a Ph.D. in philosophy, or obtain an M.A. as preparation for other professional or academic careers.
column52: $569.22/Credit Hour (Texas Resident, based on 9 credit hours)

column2: Master of Arts in Political Science
column16: Applicants must meet the following general requirements to be considered for admission to the M.A. program in political science. Meeting these requirements does not guarantee admission. A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. An undergraduate cumulative grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale over the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework (or 3.0 overall for students with less than 60 hours of undergraduate coursework). A strong letter of intent (statement of purpose). Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant’s academic and/or professional potential. A writing sample of no more than 20 pages. A background in political science, history, economics, or another relevant discipline. Minimum scores on the Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) General Test are required for students with an undergraduate GPA below 3.0. For students with an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher, the GRE is optional. International applicants must also meet UNT's English Language Proficiency requirements.
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
column47: The M.A. in Political Science offers students training in the discipline's major fields as well as an opportunity to deepen their understanding of political phenomena. Students can elect to write a thesis or complete a non-thesis option. The program is designed to prepare students for a Ph.D. program or for employment in government, think tanks, or the private sector. Students in the M.A. program take 30 hours of graduate work, including courses in American politics, comparative politics, and international relations, as well as political theory and methodology. All students must complete PSCI 5000: Political Science Research and Methods. At the completion of their coursework, students take comprehensive examinations in two of the three subfields (American politics, comparative politics, or international relations) or submit a thesis.

column2: Master of Arts in Political Science with a concentration in Advocacy, Politics and Policy
column16:
Admission to the Master of Arts program in political science is open to students holding a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must meet the following requirements for unconditional admission:
1. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 undergraduate hours.
2. A combined verbal and quantitative score of 300 on the Graduate Record Examination (GRE).
3. Two letters of recommendation from former instructors who can attest to the applicant’s academic preparedness and scholarly potential. Applicants with a period of professional work experience may substitute one letter from a professional supervisor.
4. A statement of purpose (approximately 500-700 words) describing the applicant’s academic interests and career goals. The statement should also address how the applicant’s academic and/or professional background has prepared them for graduate study in political science at UNT.
5. A writing sample demonstrating the applicant’s ability to conduct research and write an analytical essay. Typically, this is a research paper prepared for a previous political science course. No minimum or maximum length is specified, but the applicant should choose a sample that best demonstrates their writing and analytical skills.
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
column47: The Master of Arts in Political Science with a concentration in Advocacy, Politics and Policy is designed to provide students with a strong theoretical and practical understanding of political processes, public policy and advocacy. The program will equip students with the necessary skills to analyze complex political issues, develop effective advocacy strategies, and contribute to public discourse and policymaking. Students will engage with core concepts in political science, including political theory, comparative politics, international relations, and American politics, while also gaining specialized knowledge in areas such as grassroots organizing, lobbying, campaign management, and policy analysis.
column101: Competitive Scholarships, Teaching Fellowships, Assistantships, Travel Grants

column2: Master of Arts in Professional and Technical Communication
column16: Admission to the Graduate School requires a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution and a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee admission. Additional requirements for the Professional and Technical Communication MA program include: A two-page, single-spaced statement of purpose addressing your academic and professional experience and how the Professional and Technical Communication program will help you meet your career goals; An updated résumé or curriculum vitae; An academic or professional writing sample of approximately 10-20 pages; Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended; Three letters of recommendation; The GRE is not required for admission to the MA program.
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
column47: The Master of Arts in Professional and Technical Communication is an interdisciplinary degree that enables students to develop their skills as communicators, researchers, and critical thinkers. Students in the program develop practical and theoretical knowledge that prepares them for careers in fields such as: corporate communications, technical writing, editing, grant writing, digital content creation, information architecture, usability, web design, and digital publication. Students in our program also learn how to engage in ethical and critical communication across various contexts, and they learn how to apply their skills as professional communicators to a variety of workplaces and organizations. Coursework provides students with the opportunity to pursue individualized interests in a range of relevant areas, including: rhetoric, writing and editing, digital media, digital humanities, and communication for social justice.

column2: Master of Arts in Spanish
column16: An applicant must meet the university requirements for admission to graduate school as well as the following departmental requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum 3.0 GPA in 12 hours of graduate coursework. A minimum of 24 upper-level undergraduate hours in Spanish, including courses in composition, culture, civilization, literature and linguistics, with a minimum grade of B in all Spanish courses. An academic writing sample, preferably in Spanish. A statement of purpose, preferably in Spanish, describing their interest in graduate study in Spanish at UNT. A letter of recommendation (optional). Satisfactory scores on the GRE General Test, with a minimum of 145 (quantitative) and 153 (verbal) on the revised test (or equivalent on the previous test); or a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum 3.0 GPA in 12 hours of graduate coursework.
column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
column47: The M.A. program in Spanish is designed to develop in students a broad knowledge of Hispanic literatures and cultures, as well as an advanced command of the Spanish language. Students may choose either the Latin American literature and cultures option or the Peninsular literature and cultures option. Both options prepare students for doctoral work in Spanish or related fields and for careers requiring expertise in Spanish language, literature and culture. They are particularly relevant for those seeking to teach Spanish at the college or secondary level. The M.A. in Spanish requires 30 credit hours. Students may choose a thesis or non-thesis option.

column47: The Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics with a concentration in Geographic Information Systems (GIS) focuses on the principles and applications of advanced data analytics through the lens of GIS. This program is designed to provide students with the theoretical knowledge and practical skills necessary to analyze, interpret, and visualize complex spatial data using advanced analytical techniques and GIS software. Graduates will be prepared for careers in fields requiring expertise in spatial data science, geoinformatics, urban planning, environmental science, and public health, among others. The curriculum integrates core concepts of data analytics, statistics, machine learning, and data visualization with specialized courses in GIS, remote sensing, and spatial modeling. Students will engage in hands-on projects, case studies, and a culminating experience that applies their skills to real-world spatial data challenges.

This curriculum is designed to produce students with a deep knowledge of the application of data analytics, including the ethical and social implications inherent in the use of data. The program emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical applications through a rigorous curriculum that incorporates various tools and techniques such as statistical analysis, machine learning, data visualization, and predictive modeling.

Students gain a comprehensive understanding of data collection, storage, processing, analysis, interpretation, and visualization, along with the ethical considerations and privacy issues surrounding data. The program emphasizes the practical application of data analytics techniques and tools through hands-on projects and real-world case studies. Students will develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills essential for success in data-driven careers. Students in the MS in Advanced Data Analytics program may choose from one of eight concentrations designed to provide specialized knowledge and skills in particular application areas.

Students are trained to use a variety of programming languages, statistical software, and database systems. The program is designed to meet the growing demand for data scientists and analysts in a variety of industries. The program is offered fully online.

column47: The Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics is designed to train students in the most current techniques for extracting knowledge from large data sets and to provide in-depth training in the latest industry-standard software and analytical methodologies. column47: The Master of Science (M.S.) in Advanced Data Analytics program is designed for students seeking to develop advanced skills in the fields of business analytics, health analytics, applied analytics, and statistics. The program provides a strong foundation in descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics. The program prepares students for careers in fields such as data scientist, data analyst, business intelligence analyst, and analytics consultant. Students will learn to apply advanced statistical and machine learning techniques to real-world problems, interpret and communicate findings, and make data-driven decisions.

column2: Master of Science in Applied Behavior Analysis
column16: A minimum GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) in the last 60 undergraduate hours of coursework. GRE scores are not required for admission. Three (3) letters of recommendation. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. For international students, a TOEFL or IELTS score.
column47: The Master of Science program in Applied Behavior Analysis trains students in the scientific principles of behavior and their application to a wide range of human behaviors, including autism and related disabilities, behavioral medicine, education, and organizational behavior management. Students will be prepared to work in a variety of settings, including schools, clinics, homes, and organizations. Graduates of the program are eligible to apply for certification as Board Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBA) by the Behavior Analyst Certification Board® (BACB®). As a student in the Applied Behavior Analysis master’s program, you’ll learn: About the principles and methods of behavior analysis, including behavioral assessment, intervention, and research. How to apply these principles to a variety of populations and settings. The ethical and professional standards of behavior analysis. The skills to design, implement, and evaluate behavior analytic interventions. About current research and literature in applied behavior analysis.
column50: The Master of Science program in Applied Behavior Analysis at the University of North Texas includes a Verified Course Sequence (VCS) that meets the coursework requirements for eligibility to take the Board Certified Behavior Analyst® (BCBA®) Examination. This VCS has been verified by the Association for Behavior Analysis International (ABAI) and meets the requirements for eligibility to take the BCBA® Examination.

column47: The Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence (MS in AI) is an interdisciplinary degree between Computer Science and Information Science. It prepares students for a career in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. The program gives students an in-depth understanding of theoretical and practical aspects of Artificial Intelligence. Graduates will be equipped to apply AI and Machine Learning techniques in various fields through data analytics, deep learning, natural language processing, intelligent agent development, and human-computer interaction. The program emphasizes the design, development, and application of artificial intelligence techniques for solving real-world problems. The MS in AI program focuses on cutting-edge topics that empower students with the skills and knowledge to meet the rapidly growing demand for AI professionals in industry, government, and research.

column47: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Behavior Analysis at the University of North Texas is designed to provide graduate training in the experimental and applied analysis of behavior. The program helps prepare students for careers in research, teaching and practice (e.g., as Board Certified Behavior Analysts). Our program is designed for students who are interested in developing expertise in the application of behavioral principles to a wide variety of human behaviors (e.g., developmental disabilities, autism, education, child behavior, health & fitness, traumatic brain injury, organizational behavior management). As a result of this training, students will be qualified to enter various doctoral programs, teach at the university level, conduct research and work in a variety of settings applying the principles of behavior analysis. Students in the Master of Science in Behavior Analysis program will engage in course work, practicum experiences, and research that will result in the attainment of the following: Knowledge of the philosophical assumptions of behavior analysis, experimental analysis of behavior, applied behavior analysis, and professional practice. Skills in the experimental analysis of behavior, applied behavior analysis, and professional practice. Abilities to apply knowledge and skills in behavior analysis in professional and ethical ways.

column2: Master of Science in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
column16: Students must meet the admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School along with the following program-specific requirements. Three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required.
column47: A Master of Science in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology from the University of North Texas will prepare you to be a skilled and innovative professional in a wide range of biology-related careers. You will perform research in modern laboratories and acquire skills in critical thinking, experimental design, scientific methodology, data analysis and interpretation, and oral and written communication of scientific concepts. This program will provide you with a solid foundation in biochemistry and molecular biology, along with a deep understanding of experimental principles and practices. You will gain experience in a variety of laboratory techniques and technologies, including protein purification, electrophoresis, chromatography, spectroscopy, cloning, DNA sequencing, PCR, cell culture, microscopy, and bioinformatics. Our graduates pursue diverse career paths in areas such as biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, clinical research, forensics, agriculture, environmental science, and government. Many also continue their education in Ph.D. programs or medical school.

column47: The Department of Biological Sciences offers a Master of Science (MS) degree in Biology. This program is designed to provide advanced training and research opportunities in various biological disciplines. Our faculty members conduct research in areas such as cell biology, developmental biology, ecology, evolution, microbiology, molecular biology, neurobiology, plant biology, physiology and zoology. The program prepares students for further graduate study toward a doctoral degree, for careers in research, industry or government, or for teaching positions. Thesis and non-thesis options are available, though the thesis option is strongly encouraged.

column2: Master of Science in Biology with a concentration in Sub-Antarctic Biocultural Conservation
column16: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School and the following program requirements: GPA of 3.0 or better in the last 60 undergraduate credit hours (excluding developmental coursework). Official GRE scores. There is no minimum score requirement; however, competitive applicants typically score in the 50th percentile or higher on the Verbal and Quantitative sections and 3.5 or higher on the Analytical Writing section. Statement of Purpose that includes specific details regarding the applicant's research interests, experience, and why they want to pursue the MS with a concentration in Sub-Antarctic Biocultural Conservation degree at the University of North Texas. column47: The Master of Science (MS) in Biology with a concentration in Sub-Antarctic Biocultural Conservation is a joint program offered in collaboration with the University of Magallanes, Chile (UMAG) and the Millennium Institute of Ecology and Biogeography (IEB). The program is designed to provide students with advanced knowledge and practical skills in biological and sociocultural conservation issues relevant to the Sub-Antarctic region. Students will engage in interdisciplinary coursework, research, and fieldwork, fostering a deep understanding of the unique ecosystems and cultural heritage of the Sub-Antarctic. The curriculum emphasizes a biocultural approach, integrating biological sciences with social sciences and humanities to address complex conservation challenges. Graduates will be prepared for careers in academia, research, non-governmental organizations, government agencies, and other institutions focused on conservation, sustainable development, and environmental policy in polar and sub-polar regions.

column47: The Master of Science in Biomedical Engineering program prepares students to meet the growing need for highly qualified engineers in the medical device, biotechnology, and pharmaceutical industries. Students in the program will be exposed to coursework and research covering areas such as medical imaging, neural engineering, biomaterials, biomechanics, biomedical instrumentation, drug delivery, and computational biology. The program emphasizes both foundational biomedical engineering principles and practical applications through hands-on research and design projects. Graduates of the program will be well-prepared for advanced careers in industry, research, or further doctoral studies.

Applicants must satisfy the admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School and the following departmental requirements: Applicants must have a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 undergraduate hours and a 3.0 in undergraduate chemistry courses. column47:
The Department of Chemistry offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy degrees. Graduate studies emphasize research that expands the understanding of all aspects of chemistry and its application to other fields of science.
The Master of Science in chemistry provides students with the advanced knowledge and skills necessary to pursue careers in industry, government, or academia, or to prepare for further doctoral study in chemistry or related fields. The program offers thesis and non-thesis options, allowing students to tailor their degree plan to their individual goals and interests. Students will develop a strong foundation in advanced chemical principles, laboratory techniques, and scientific communication.

column2: Master of Science in Computer Engineering
column16: Applicants must meet the admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School and the College of Engineering. In addition to meeting the standard requirements, applicants must also provide: Official Transcripts, Statement of Purpose, Résumé, and Three letters of recommendation. column47: The master’s degree in computer engineering prepares students for leadership roles in industry, government and education. Our multidisciplinary approach draws on the expertise of faculty in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering and the Department of Electrical Engineering. This enables students to combine courses from both disciplines to tailor a master’s program that meets their career goals. You’ll gain knowledge and skills in areas such as computer architecture, digital system design, embedded systems, very large scale integration (VLSI) design, testing, computer networks, digital signal processing, distributed processing, network-on-chip, VLSI circuit design and data communication. As a student in the program, you’ll be able to participate in a variety of research projects. Many faculty members in computer engineering are conducting research in areas such as embedded and real-time systems, VLSI design, fault-tolerant computing, computer networks, wireless networks, network security, computer architecture and performance evaluation.

Applicants must provide official scores for the GRE General Test, taken within the last five years. There are no minimum GRE scores required for admission to the MS program. However, students who score below the 30th percentile on any of the three sections (verbal, quantitative, analytical writing) will be denied regular admission and will be subject to conditional admission, as described below, or denied admission.

column47:

Students completing the program may become licensed professional counselors, school counselors, or registered play therapists in Texas. Our program is a Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) accredited program in Clinical Mental Health Counseling and School Counseling. We focus on preparing professional counselors who are grounded in theory, research, and best practices. As a student, you will have the opportunity to engage in meaningful scholarly discourse and fieldwork experiences within a supportive and collaborative environment.
column50: Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) accredited program in Clinical Mental Health Counseling and School Counseling.

Students with baccalaureate degrees in other fields (e.g., business, history) are encouraged to apply, but may be required to take up to 12 semester credit hours of undergraduate criminal justice courses (e.g., CJUS 3100, CJUS 3200, CJUS 3300, CJUS 3400) prior to being unconditionally admitted to the program. Applicants must meet the general admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School. column47: The Master of Science in Information Science (MSIS) program provides advanced graduate education for professionals in the field of information science. Information science is an interdisciplinary field that seeks to understand, analyze, and manage information in various forms and contexts. It draws on theories and practices from computer science, cognitive science, library science, and other disciplines to address the challenges and opportunities of the information age. The program offers a range of specializations allowing students to tailor their studies to their interests and career goals. Concentrations include archival studies, data science, digital content and information management, health informatics, human-computer interaction, information organization, information systems, knowledge management, metadata and discovery, school library media, sport entertainment information and analytics, storage and preservation, and user experience design. The MSIS program is designed for students with a bachelor's degree in any field who are interested in pursuing a career in information science. It is also suitable for professionals who wish to enhance their skills and knowledge in this rapidly evolving field. Graduates of the program are prepared for a variety of roles in information science, including information architects, data analysts, knowledge managers, user experience designers, and information consultants. The program emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and practical skills development, enabling students to address real-world challenges in diverse information environments. The MSIS program is an online program.

The program provides the theoretical and practical knowledge base for students seeking careers in academic, clinical, and applied settings. The program provides the knowledge, skills, and dispositions necessary to design, develop, implement, and evaluate effective learning environments and experiences in various contexts. The coursework provides students with a strong theoretical foundation in learning, instructional design, and human performance improvement, and practical skills in instructional technology. The graduates of the program are able to apply appropriate research and evaluation methods to improve learning and performance.

column16: A master's degree in linguistics, either the M.A. or the M.S., requires prior preparation equivalent to an undergraduate minor in linguistics. Applicants are expected to be familiar with the fundamentals of linguistic analysis at the advanced undergraduate level, including phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, and historical linguistics. In addition, applicants are required to submit the following materials directly to the Department of Linguistics: Three letters of recommendation. A statement of purpose indicating the applicant’s academic interests, career goals, and reasons for pursuing graduate study in linguistics. A writing sample that demonstrates the applicant’s ability to conduct scholarly research and write clearly and analytically. Official transcripts from all universities attended. GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores, if available. (Note: GRE scores are not required for admission to the MA/MS in Linguistics programs). Additional requirements for international students can be found here.
column47: The Department of Linguistics offers a Master of Science degree in Linguistics. This degree program is designed to provide graduate training in linguistic analysis and theory, as well as in the various subfields of linguistics. Our program offers excellent training in core linguistic areas and in more specialized areas such as computational linguistics, field linguistics, and language documentation, second language acquisition, and corpus linguistics. As a graduate student, you will have the opportunity to work closely with faculty mentors, develop your own research interests, and contribute to the vibrant intellectual life of our department.

column47: The Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Computational Linguistics (M.S.) focuses on a multidisciplinary approach to the automatic processing of human language, drawing on the fields of linguistics, computer science, and library and information sciences. Students receive a thorough grounding in all aspects of linguistic science and computational analysis as it applies to natural language. Students will become familiar with current trends in computational linguistics and apply computational linguistic techniques in courses within the Department of Linguistics, the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, and the Department of Information Science. Additionally, students gain experience with a wide variety of tools and methodologies and develop the skills needed to design, implement, and evaluate solutions for a wide range of problems involving natural language. The program prepares students for careers in industry (e.g., text analytics, natural language processing, data science, language technology development) and for continued graduate study at the doctoral level.

column47: The Department of Linguistics offers both a Master of Arts (M.A.) and a Master of Science (M.S.) in Linguistics. Within the M.A. and M.S. degrees, students can choose to pursue concentrations in Computational Linguistics, Language Documentation, or TESOL. The M.A. degree provides students with a broad knowledge of language and linguistics and prepares them to teach English as a second language, teach linguistics at a community college, or pursue further graduate work in linguistics. The M.S. degree is similar to the M.A., but it also provides students with a stronger background in quantitative methods and prepares them for careers in language-related industries, such as computational linguistics, natural language processing, or language documentation. Students are required to take a set of core courses, including phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. Students will also complete a capstone project that allows them to apply their knowledge to a real-world problem or research question. The M.A. and M.S. in Linguistics degrees are designed to provide students with a strong foundation in linguistic theory and methods, as well as opportunities for specialized study in areas such as computational linguistics, language documentation, and TESOL. Students will develop critical thinking, research, and communication skills, preparing them for diverse careers or further academic pursuits.

Admission to the Mathematics (M.S.) program with a Mathematics Education Concentration is a two-step process:

Step 1: Apply to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School

Requirements for ALL graduate applicants include:

column47: The Mathematics Education Concentration is designed for students who want to continue their study of mathematics and mathematics education beyond the undergraduate level. Students will gain advanced knowledge in a variety of mathematical topics. In addition, students will learn to apply research-based pedagogical content knowledge in teaching mathematics effectively. They will also learn about current issues, trends and research in mathematics education. Our graduate courses are offered in a flexible format, with opportunities for students to study face-to-face, online or in a blended fashion. Many of our courses are offered at convenient evening hours, making it possible for students who work full-time to complete the program. Students may complete the degree entirely online as well.

This online program will equip you with the skills to address the social, psychological, and vocational impact of disabilities on individuals and their families. Throughout the UNT M.S. in Rehabilitation Counseling program, you will develop a deep understanding of disabilities and their impact, as well as the counseling techniques to support individuals in achieving their goals. The curriculum covers a wide range of topics, including: Disability and rehabilitation, Counseling theories and techniques, Assessment and evaluation, Vocational rehabilitation, Case management, Ethical and legal issues in rehabilitation, Group counseling, Family counseling, Career development, Research and program evaluation.
column50: The Master of Science in Rehabilitation Counseling program is accredited by the Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP).

column2: Master of Science in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering
column16: Candidates for the MS in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering must meet the following requirements to be admitted to the program: Official GRE scores, Three letters of recommendation, A statement of purpose, Official transcripts, Undergraduate GPA, Minimum GRE scores (146 Verbal, 146 Quantitative, 3.5 Analytical Writing). A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 overall and 3.0 in the last 60 undergraduate credit hours. Three letters of recommendation. A statement of purpose (500-1000 words). Official GRE scores: minimum of 146 Verbal, 146 Quantitative, and 3.5 Analytical Writing. column47: The Master of Science (MS) program in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering (SME) is designed to educate students on fundamental principles and knowledge pertaining to semiconductor manufacturing process integration, device and circuit design, and manufacturing and industrial engineering. Students will gain knowledge in semiconductor manufacturing processes, semiconductor device physics, process control, cleanroom operations, testing and reliability, and the economics of manufacturing, and will learn to apply these principles to solve complex problems in the semiconductor industry. The semiconductor manufacturing industry has been expanding at a rapid pace and is expected to continue this growth for decades. The US CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 provides billions in funding for domestic semiconductor manufacturing and R&D, creating a need for a highly skilled workforce across the entire supply chain. Graduates of this program will be prepared to fill critical roles in semiconductor manufacturing, research and development, and management within the semiconductor industry, contributing to the economic growth of the DFW metroplex, the state of Texas, and the nation.

Our graduates work in a variety of settings, including public schools, hospitals, rehabilitation centers, and private practices. After completing the MS degree, students are eligible to apply for Texas state licensure and national certification from the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA). Students who do not have an undergraduate degree in communication sciences and disorders may be admitted into the program. These students must complete undergraduate prerequisites prior to beginning graduate-level courses. These prerequisites can be completed at UNT as a post-baccalaureate student or at another university. If you have questions about prerequisites, please email us at shs-advising@unt.edu.
column50: The Master of Science in Speech-Language Pathology program at UNT is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA), 2200 Research Boulevard #310, Rockville, Maryland 20850, 800-498-2071 or 301-296-5700. This program will develop skills in the areas of tax planning, tax compliance, tax research, tax technology and data analytics. This includes developing and interpreting data models, data visualization, and the ability to apply current and emerging data analytic techniques to solve taxation problems. This program combines both tax and data analytics courses within the G. Brint Ryan College of Business and the College of Engineering. Upon completion of this program, students will be prepared for careers in public accounting, corporate taxation, and governmental agencies, and will be able to sit for the CPA exam in Texas.

column47: The Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.) program at the University of North Texas is a four-year clinical doctorate designed to prepare students for professional practice in audiology. The curriculum meets the academic and clinical requirements for licensure as an audiologist in Texas and for national certification by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA). The program provides students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences related to hearing and balance, as well as extensive clinical training in all areas of audiology. Students complete a minimum of 75 semester credit hours of academic coursework and 2000 hours of supervised clinical experience, including a full-time externship during the fourth year. Our students gain clinical experience in a variety of specialty areas including cochlear implants, pediatrics, educational audiology, and private practice settings. Students also have the opportunity to engage in research across a wide range of interests including electrophysiology, psychoacoustics, speech perception, hearing aids, and vestibular assessment. The UNT Au.D. program is committed to excellence in education, research, and clinical practice, preparing students to be leaders in the field of audiology.

column38: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
column47: The Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) is a professional doctorate designed for senior managers and executives seeking to apply advanced academic theory and rigorous research to practical business problems. Unlike a Ph.D. program, which primarily prepares graduates for academic research careers, the DBA focuses on developing scholar-practitioners who can bridge the gap between academic theory and real-world business challenges. The UNT DBA program emphasizes research that directly contributes to business practice, policy, and strategy. Our graduates are equipped to lead organizational change, innovate business models, and address complex problems with data-driven insights. They often pursue roles in senior management, consulting, or specialized research within corporations, government, or non-profit organizations.

column2: Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) in Performance
column16: The DMA program is designed for the highly talented musician who has demonstrated exceptional promise through previous academic degrees and performance. It is a three-year residency degree that combines comprehensive coursework and intensive instruction for the highest artistic and academic achievement. Areas of study include Music History, Music Theory, and other music-related courses. Students seeking the DMA degree must audition for entrance, in addition to meeting the standard UNT TGS and College of Music requirements. All graduate applicants must meet the UNT Graduate School’s general admission requirements: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution; Minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 undergraduate credit hours or a 3.0 on all undergraduate work; Official transcripts from all universities attended; Official scores for English Language Proficiency (ELP), if required (International applicants); Official GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores, if required by your program of interest. Graduate students wishing to apply to any degree program in the College of Music must complete two applications: the UNT Toulouse Graduate School application and the College of Music graduate application. In addition to the online application, applicants must submit the following materials directly to the College of Music (via the online application form): Curriculum Vitae/Resume – an overview of your academic and performance/professional experience; Statement of Purpose – a statement of your academic and professional goals, including a discussion of your interest in the UNT College of Music. (Maximum of 500 words). DMA applicants must also submit (in addition to the above): Repertoire List – a representative list of your previous performance repertoire; Writing Sample (DMA Performance only) – a paper written on a musical topic (e.g., from a music history/theory course); Interview/Audition.

column47: The DMA in Performance is the most advanced music performance degree offered at UNT, preparing students for careers as performing musicians and artist-teachers at the highest level. Students develop expertise in their principal applied area of study, gaining a breadth of knowledge across music history, theory, and literature, and a deep understanding of repertoire. Throughout the program, students refine their musical and technical skills, interpretative abilities, and scholarly research while developing a distinctive artistic voice. Opportunities abound for students to perform as soloists, in chamber ensembles, and in large ensembles in a wide range of styles, genres, and historical periods. Students receive intensive private instruction, participate in master classes, and have access to UNT’s world-class facilities and performance venues. Upon completion of the DMA in Performance, students will be prepared to assume positions in college/university music departments, professional symphony orchestras, opera companies, touring ensembles, and other performance venues.

The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Art Education at the University of North Texas provides an advanced course of study that is focused on art education as a broad field of inquiry and practice, including, but not limited to, K-12 schooling contexts, post-secondary education, museums and community arts organizations. The curriculum is designed to educate scholars who will contribute to research, theory, policy and practice in art education locally, nationally and globally.

The faculty members in the Department of Art Education and Art History are active researchers, practitioners and educators whose work reflects an extensive range of approaches to research, diverse theoretical and methodological perspectives, and varied areas of emphasis related to learning and teaching in art. Faculty interests include critical studies, social justice, curriculum development, culturally responsive pedagogy, teacher education, community art education, visual culture, disability studies, and contemporary art practices in education. Students are encouraged to pursue an individualized course of study that aligns with their intellectual interests and professional aspirations within the broad scope of the field of art education. The program emphasizes both disciplinary breadth and individualized depth through a flexible curriculum of foundational studies, advanced seminars and independent research.

Our faculty members are highly collaborative and committed to mentoring students in both experimental and theoretical approaches. Students gain hands-on experience in cutting-edge techniques and instrumentation, preparing them for successful careers in academia, industry, and government. The program culminates in the completion and defense of a doctoral dissertation based on original research.

column47:
A Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Business from the G. Brint Ryan College of Business at the University of North Texas prepares you for a career as a university professor and researcher. As a student in the program, you will develop expertise in research methods and theories, and learn how to conduct independent and original research. You will learn how to produce high-quality scholarly research in your primary concentration, enabling you to contribute to knowledge generation and dissemination. A Ph.D. in Business from UNT enables you to make a significant impact on your field of study. Upon graduating, you will be prepared for a career at a research-intensive institution as a tenure-track faculty member. Our graduates typically find placements at AACSB-accredited business schools in the U.S. and around the world.

Admission to the program is highly selective, and applicants are expected to have an outstanding academic record, competitive GRE or GMAT scores, strong letters of recommendation, and a demonstrated interest in pursuing academic research. The program is full-time, requiring a significant commitment of time and effort over four to five years to complete. Students are required to take 69 credit hours for the PhD. After the first year, students can apply for an in-residence master’s degree, which usually requires them to take 30 credits to meet the requirements of the master's degree. Students are typically provided with financial support, which includes a stipend and tuition waiver, in exchange for working as a teaching or research assistant. The financial support package also typically includes health insurance.

To learn more about individual concentrations and their requirements, please visit the G. Brint Ryan College of Business website.

The program emphasizes the development of research and scholarship skills, and provides students with a broad understanding of the historical, philosophical, political, social, cultural, and economic foundations of higher education, as well as the organizational and leadership dimensions of colleges and universities. Areas of study include, but are not limited to, student affairs administration, college teaching, higher education management, higher education finance, higher education law, and the history and philosophy of higher education. The program also offers opportunities for individualized study through electives, independent studies, and dissertation research. The Ph.D. in Higher Education requires a minimum of 66 semester hours beyond the master’s degree, including 15 hours of core courses, 15 hours of research courses, 15 hours of electives, and 21 hours of dissertation. All students complete a doctoral qualifying examination prior to beginning dissertation work. All degree requirements must be completed within a period of 10 years.

column47:
Computational linguistics is an interdisciplinary field between computer science and linguistics. It focuses on developing computer models of natural language to solve language-related problems. Examples of computational linguistics applications include spell checking, grammar checking, machine translation, spam filtering, text summarization, speech recognition, and information extraction.
The Certificate in Computational Linguistics at UNT is designed for students who are interested in developing advanced computational linguistics skills. The certificate targets graduate students in linguistics, computer science, and related areas. Our curriculum offers a solid foundation in computational linguistics theory and applications with a balance between theoretical and practical training. We encourage students to gain hands-on experience by completing projects on authentic computational linguistics problems using real-world data and open-source software tools.
Upon completing the certificate program, students will be able to demonstrate:
*   Solid understanding of computational linguistics theory and applications
*   Ability to implement computational linguistics techniques to solve real-world problems
*   Experience using open-source computational linguistics software tools
*   Skills in evaluating computational linguistics systems
