A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution with an adequate undergraduate GPA (generally, a minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale in the last 60 undergraduate hours and any graduate work). 2. Undergraduate preparation for the certificate program is satisfied by earning a bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, data science, information science, mathematics, statistics or a related field. 3. Students who have not earned a bachelor's degree in a related field may be admitted to the certificate program provisionally upon recommendation of the department. These students will be required to demonstrate competency through examinations, coursework or other evidence in the following areas: calculus, linear algebra, basic probability and statistics, data structures, and object-oriented programming. 4. Students must submit the following directly to the Toulouse Graduate School: Official transcripts from all universities attended. GRE is not required for this certificate. A statement of purpose outlining academic interests, relevant experience and career goals. A current resume or CV. Two letters of recommendation (optional but recommended).
column47: Data scientists are in high demand and needed across industries. Become a part of this growing field through the University of North Texas’ online Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Science. As a student in this program, you will develop the knowledge and skills necessary to prepare you for careers in data science. Our courses cover topics such as data visualization, data mining, machine learning, deep learning, statistical analysis, and programming. Through the Data Science Graduate Academic Certificate, you will learn to apply computational and statistical analysis to large data sets. Other topics include: Data collection and cleansing, Data visualization, Data mining, Data-driven decision making, Machine learning, Deep learning, Statistical analysis, Programming, Natural Language Processing, Artificial intelligence.

column2: Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Communication Analytics
column16: Admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Communication Analytics is granted through the Toulouse Graduate School. Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. No GRE required.

column47: As the digital landscape expands, the ability to analyze and interpret data from online communication channels becomes increasingly vital for organizations. The Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Communication Analytics is designed to equip students with the skills to strategically collect, analyze, and apply data to improve digital communication strategies. This certificate offers a focused curriculum that covers areas such as web analytics, social media analytics, data visualization, and ethical considerations in data analysis. Graduates will be prepared to leverage data-driven insights to optimize campaigns, enhance user engagement, and make informed decisions in a variety of communication-related roles. This certificate is ideal for professionals seeking to advance their careers in marketing, public relations, corporate communication, or related fields, and who wish to specialize in the analytical aspects of digital communication.

column16: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School and specific requirements for the certificate. Applicants who do not meet the minimum GPA may be admitted to the certificate program on probation by the department. column47: The graduate academic certificate in Digital Content Management prepares students for a career in the dynamic field of digital content. The program will provide students with competencies to create, manage, preserve and disseminate digital content and assets for various types of organizations using a variety of formats and platforms. Students will acquire the skills necessary to identify and implement best practices for digital content creation, acquisition, and curation. The certificate can be completed in conjunction with an M.S. degree in Information Science or as a stand-alone certificate.

column2: Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Curation and Data Management
column16: To be admitted to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Curation and Data Management, you must meet the following requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. A minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in all graduate work. The GRE is not required for admission to this certificate program. column47: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Curation and Data Management addresses the growing demand for professionals skilled in managing digital assets throughout their lifecycle. This 12-hour certificate program provides students with the foundational knowledge and practical skills needed to curate, preserve, and provide access to digital data in various institutional settings. Students will learn about data governance, metadata standards, digital preservation strategies, and the ethical considerations involved in managing digital information. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on experience with relevant tools and technologies, preparing graduates for roles in libraries, archives, museums, government agencies, and corporate environments. The certificate is suitable for current information professionals seeking to enhance their skills, as well as for graduate students interested in specializing in digital curation and data management.

column47: This certificate is an 18-credit-hour program offered through the Department of Merchandising and Digital Retailing. Students will gain an understanding of current technologies and strategies used in digital retail, including data analytics, social media marketing, and omnichannel retailing. This certificate is designed for individuals seeking to enhance their skills for career advancement or those who wish to transition into the fast-paced and evolving digital retail industry. The certificate can also be stacked to meet degree requirements for the Master of Science in Merchandising. A 3.0 GPA is required for all certificate courses. column38: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
column47: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Social Science introduces graduate students to the skills necessary to conduct research and analyze digital social data using computational methods. Students will gain practical experience with various computational tools and techniques, including data collection, data management, data analysis, and data visualization. Upon completion of the certificate, students will be equipped to analyze digital social data, interpret their findings, and communicate their results effectively.

column47: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Energy Accounting provides professional development for energy industry accountants and auditors to enhance their knowledge in the complex area of energy accounting. The certificate will address issues related to oil and gas, utilities, alternative energy and environmental accounting. The certificate consists of 12 graduate credit hours. Graduates of the program will be able to: Demonstrate an understanding of current financial accounting, auditing and taxation issues applicable to companies in the energy industry. Demonstrate knowledge of current issues in financial reporting as it applies to the energy industry. Demonstrate an understanding of internal controls and risk management issues in the energy industry. Demonstrate an understanding of ethical issues within the energy industry.

column2: Graduate Academic Certificate in Energy
column16: To be admitted to the Energy Graduate Academic Certificate program, a student must meet the following criteria: Hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. column47: UNT's Department of Energy and Environmental Policy (ENEP) offers a Graduate Academic Certificate in Energy. Students interested in energy policy have a unique opportunity to gain knowledge and experience in energy issues and policy. The certificate can be standalone or complement another graduate degree. The certificate requires 12 credit hours (4 courses). The certificate program allows students to specialize in areas relating to energy, renewable energy, and fossil fuels. Students gain foundational knowledge and understanding of energy-related topics across multiple disciplines. Courses cover topics such as: U.S. and international energy policy, energy demand, energy economics, renewable energy, energy conservation, environmental issues, and energy security. The Graduate Academic Certificate in Energy provides students with the foundational knowledge and skills in current energy issues that are critical in today's energy landscape. These skills are highly valued by employers in both the private and public sector.

column2: Graduate Academic Certificate in Environmental Ethics and Science
column16: For admission, students must have been admitted to a graduate degree program in Philosophy, Environmental Science, or a related field; or, if not seeking a graduate degree, have a 3.0 overall undergraduate GPA and apply directly to the certificate program via the Toulouse Graduate School. column38: Department of Philosophy, College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
column47: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Environmental Ethics and Science introduces students to the core philosophical concepts, theories and debates in environmental ethics, and provides students with basic training in environmental science. The Certificate integrates ethical theory, policy, and scientific method, and is designed to provide students with the interdisciplinary knowledge and skills needed for a variety of occupations that require both scientific literacy and ethical problem solving related to the environment. The Certificate serves a wide range of students including those working in federal or state government, NGOs, and the private sector; current or prospective graduate students who wish to add a credential in environmental ethics and science; and individuals who wish to pursue the Certificate as a stand-alone credential. The Certificate requires 15 credit hours of graduate course work (9 hours in philosophy courses and 6 hours in environmental science courses) and can be completed in approximately 1.5-2 years.

column2: Graduate Academic Certificate in Event Management

column47: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Event Management provides comprehensive training and knowledge necessary to successfully plan, implement, and manage a wide range of events. This certificate is designed for professionals seeking to enhance their careers in the event planning industry, or for individuals looking to gain specialized knowledge in this growing field. The program emphasizes strategic planning, operational logistics, risk management, marketing, and sustainability in event contexts. Students will learn how to design, execute, and evaluate various types of events, including corporate meetings, conferences, festivals, and social gatherings. The curriculum also covers budgeting, vendor negotiations, sponsorship acquisition, and the application of technology in event management. Graduates will be equipped with the skills and expertise to pursue leadership roles in event management, hospitality, tourism, and related sectors.

column47: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Gender, Feminism, and Environmental Justice (GFEJ) is designed for students who want to develop skills and knowledge to engage in scholarly research, public policy, and advocacy that addresses the gendered and racialized dimensions of environmental problems and environmental movements. The certificate is housed in the Department of Women's and Gender Studies and is available to all graduate students at UNT as well as post-baccalaureate students not currently enrolled in a UNT graduate program. Students must apply for admission to the certificate program. Current graduate students who wish to add the certificate may do so by submitting a certificate application to the Toulouse Graduate School after completing at least 9 credit hours toward their graduate degree and having a minimum 3.0 graduate GPA. Non-degree seeking students may apply to the Toulouse Graduate School as post-baccalaureate students.

Have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 in undergraduate work. Submit a current resume or curriculum vitae highlighting previous academic training and/or relevant experience. column47: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Geographic Information Systems (GIS) is designed for those who wish to enhance their skills in GIS science and technology. This certificate is beneficial for individuals currently in a graduate program who wish to strengthen their GIS skills, or for individuals not currently in a graduate program but desire to obtain graduate-level GIS skills for career enhancement. The certificate is offered through the School of Public Health. Students completing the certificate may be interested in pursuing careers in Public Health, Environmental Science, Urban Planning, Emergency Management, etc.

column2: Graduate Academic Certificate in Health Data Science
column16:
Admission to the GAC in Health Data Science is restricted to applicants who have been admitted to a master’s or doctoral degree program in the College of Health and Public Service (HPS) or the College of Engineering (COE) at UNT. column47: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Health Data Science provides students with the foundational knowledge and skills necessary for working with health data, and for understanding and applying data science methods in the health domain. The courses cover essential topics in health data science, including health care data formats, privacy regulations, data analysis, machine learning applications, and ethical considerations. The program aims to prepare professionals for careers in health care analytics, research, and public health, equipping them to leverage data-driven insights to improve health outcomes and inform decision-making. Students will gain practical experience through projects and case studies, developing a portfolio of work relevant to the health data science field. The program is designed for individuals with a background in computer science, statistics, health sciences, or a related field, who wish to specialize in the growing area of health data science. The certificate is offered primarily online.

column47: The Graduate Academic Certificate (GAC) in Health Information is designed to provide health care professionals and individuals with a background in health care or information technology with an opportunity to acquire knowledge and skills to lead and manage the increasingly complex information technology landscape in health care organizations. The health information industry continues to expand as providers transition to digital medical records, and the health care system relies more heavily on data for decision making. These trends are fueling a demand for professionals with knowledge and skills in health information to fill a variety of roles within hospitals, medical practices, health insurance companies, public health agencies, and pharmaceutical companies. The certificate program will prepare professionals to fill roles in the areas of health informatics, health information technology, health information management, and public health informatics. The curriculum focuses on health information standards, health IT infrastructure, health data analytics, and information privacy, security, and ethics. The 15-hour certificate provides a solid foundation of knowledge and skills that can be completed as a standalone certificate or as part of the Master of Science in Information Science (MSIS) or other graduate degree programs at UNT. This certificate can be completed fully online.

column2: Graduate Academic Certificate in Health Services Administration

The curriculum is designed for working professionals seeking to advance their careers in healthcare administration.

The program consists of 15 credit hours of graduate-level coursework. The curriculum includes courses in healthcare policy, financial management, strategic planning, and human resources. Students will also complete a capstone project or internship, allowing them to apply their knowledge and skills in a real-world healthcare setting.

Upon completion of the certificate, students will be prepared to assume leadership roles in various healthcare organizations. Graduates will have the skills and knowledge to manage complex healthcare organizations, lead teams, and make sound financial decisions. The certificate is also an excellent option for students interested in pursuing a master's degree in health services administration or a related field.

Completion of a graduate admission application through the ApplyTexas portal and payment of the nonrefundable application fee. Additional application documents required for the G.A.C. in Learning Analytics (in addition to the application listed above): No GRE required, Statement of Purpose, 3 Letters of Recommendation, Current Resume/Curriculum Vitae.
column47: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Learning Analytics provides students with knowledge and skills to understand how to collect, analyze, and report data related to learner and learning contexts in order to improve learning processes and outcomes. Learning Analytics is a growing area that has broad application in corporate, government, military, non-profit, and academic settings. The program is designed for graduate students and working professionals seeking to add expertise in learning analytics to their existing academic or professional skill sets. Students will learn the process of learning analytics from data collection to reporting, including data manipulation, visualization, statistical analysis, and ethical considerations. The program offers a core set of skills and competencies in learning analytics, but also allows students to customize their program of study to meet their own interests and career goals. The certificate is offered completely online.

column2: Graduate Academic Certificate in Learning Sciences
column16: Admission to the learning technologies master's, doctoral and graduate academic certificate programs is a two-step process. In order to be admitted to the graduate certificate program, you must: 1. Meet the admission requirements for the UNT Toulouse Graduate School. 2. Meet the program-specific admission requirements for the graduate academic certificate in learning sciences or graduate academic certificate in instructional systems. Program-Specific Requirements for all Learning Technologies Graduate Programs (M.S., Ph.D., Graduate Academic Certificates) include: Statement of Purpose: Submit a 500-word statement describing your academic and professional background, goals, and how the program aligns with those goals. Resume/CV: Submit a current resume or curriculum vitae. Three Letters of Recommendation: Provide three letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to your academic and/or professional capabilities. GRE Test Scores (Optional): GRE General Test scores (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing) are optional for all Learning Technologies graduate programs. If you choose to submit scores, they may strengthen your application.
column47: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Learning Sciences is designed to help students better understand how humans learn across a variety of contexts and age groups. This certificate is designed for a variety of students, including those who wish to enhance their professional skills in learning and development within their current professional careers, those pursuing advanced graduate degrees in various fields related to learning, and those interested in pursuing additional knowledge within the learning sciences field. The Certificate in Learning Sciences does not lead to educator certification.

column2: Graduate Academic Certificate in Narrative Journalism
column16: An earned master’s degree from an accredited institution. In some cases, a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution will be sufficient. Undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work. Graduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on all graduate work. Upload a personal statement discussing academic and professional goals relevant to the field of narrative journalism (500 words). Upload a résumé/curriculum vitae (CV) Upload a writing sample that demonstrates the applicant’s ability to tell a story through narrative nonfiction. This can be published or unpublished material. (This is generally 10-15 pages for graduate students, but can be longer if needed to showcase your best work). All official transcripts must be sent from previously attended institutions directly to UNT. Three letters of recommendation. International applicants may be required to submit proof of English language proficiency. GRE is not required.
column47: The Narrative Journalism Certificate is a 12-hour graduate academic certificate designed to prepare students to create compelling, in-depth non-fiction stories in both print and digital forms. The certificate is offered through the Mayborn School of Journalism and can be completed as a stand-alone certificate or in conjunction with a master’s degree in journalism. It is open to any graduate student at UNT. The certificate prepares students to work as journalists, editors, communications professionals or storytellers for a wide variety of outlets. Students will learn how to write feature stories, profiles, in-depth reports, and memoirs using journalistic reporting and research methods. Students will learn how to structure long-form narratives, how to gather information through interviews and observations, and how to effectively write for various media.

column47: The Graduate Academic Certificate (GAC) in Proposal Writing is an 18-credit hour program designed to help students develop the critical writing, research, and project management skills needed to effectively secure funding from government agencies, corporations, foundations, and other funding organizations. column47: The Public Relations graduate academic certificate program is designed for students seeking to deepen their knowledge in public relations or to add public relations skills to their existing graduate studies. Students will develop a strong foundation in public relations principles, research, strategy, and communication techniques across various platforms. The certificate also emphasizes the ethical responsibilities of public relations professionals and the evolving landscape of digital media.

column47: This certificate is designed for graduate students who wish to develop expertise in qualitative research methods beyond their primary degree program requirements or for professionals who want to enhance their research skills. Participants will gain practical experience through hands-on projects and fieldwork, preparing them to conduct rigorous and impactful qualitative research in academic, professional, and community settings.

All applicants must meet the UNT Graduate School’s general admission requirements. In addition, applicants to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering program must meet the following program-specific admissions requirements: An earned bachelor’s degree in a STEM field of Engineering (e.g. Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Computer Engineering, Industrial Engineering, etc.), Physics, Chemistry, Computer Science, or similar fields from a regionally accredited institution. An undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher. For international applicants, a TOEFL score of at least 79 (internet-based) or IELTS score of at least 6.5. Resume. Statement of Purpose (up to 500 words). However, applications will be accepted until the final deadlines or until the program is full. For any questions regarding the application process, please contact us at ET-GradStudies@unt.edu.
column47: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue a career in the semiconductor manufacturing industry. The program covers topics such as semiconductor device physics, fabrication processes, characterization techniques, and packaging. Students will gain hands-on experience through laboratory work and projects, preparing them for the challenges of working in a dynamic and rapidly evolving industry. This certificate can be pursued as a stand-alone credential or as part of a master’s degree program in related engineering fields at UNT.

The Certificate in TESOL also includes a practicum component that provides hands-on teaching experience for students to apply their knowledge.
